summary: Package deployable services as production container images and publish them to GitHub Container Registry after CI passes.
description: Package the API or app as a multi-stage, non-root image with a healthcheck, then publish versioned images to GitHub Container Registry after CI. The instructions adapt to the selected stack, including an API and static site in one image for astro-fullstack. Local verification builds the image and checks that it starts healthy. Choosing a host, configuring runtime secrets and rolling out containers remain separate deployment work.
seoDescription: Build non-root production container images with healthchecks and publish versioned artifacts to GHCR through GitHub Actions.

projectExamples.title: Containerized Python API
projectExamples.description: A Python API shipped as one small image that runs without root and reports its health, published to GitHub Container Registry for each release.

projectExamples.title: Single-image site and API
projectExamples.description: An Astro site with interactive React islands calling a Node API, all served from one container image on the same origin.

plain.whatItIs: Packages the app or API as a container, a sealed bundle with what it needs, and publishes it to GitHub after checks pass.
goodAt: Building images that leave out development tools and secrets
Publishing versioned images after the project's checks pass
notGoodAt: Starting the images on a live server; pick a host and set that up separately.
